summary: Sakda Hemthep is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed an MPhil at Cardiff University by 2014, studying under his supervisor Max Deeg.

Sakunoshin Motoda was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kenyon College (circa 1888–1891), Columbia University (circa 1892–1893), and the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1893–1895). He held a post at Rikkyo University from circa 1899 to 1920.
Sakutaro Fujioka worked in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1894 to 1897 and later held a post there from circa 1906 to 1910.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga studied under numerous teachers, including Khenpo Appey and Tenzin Gyatso. He founded the Sakya Centre, Sakya College, and Sakya Institute, and served as abbot at Sakya Monastery until 2017.

A scholar in religious and Buddhist studies, Sakyong Mipham studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Dilgo Khyentse, and others, also attending Namdroling Monastery and Oxford. He succeeded Chögyam Trungpa and was a board member at Naropa University until 2018.

Sallie B. King specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied at the University of British Columbia (circa 1971–1975) under Leon Hurvitz and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University from circa 1991 to 2016.

Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Sally J. Sutherland Goldman earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley by 1979, supervised by Shivram Dattatray Joshi. She also studied under Shrinivasa Shastri and held posts at UC Berkeley (attested 1996, 2007).
Sally McAra is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed an MA at the University of Auckland from 1999 to 2000, supervised by Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.

Sally Mellick Cutler specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford by 1993 and served as office manager for the Pali Text Society (attested 1996–1997).

Salomon Lefmann was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at Münster, Heidelberg, Berlin (under Franz Bopp), and Paris, he held posts at the University of Heidelberg from 1866 as Extraordinariat für Sanskrit, associate professor (1870), and honorary professor (1901).

Sam van Schaik works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Manchester (circa 1995–2000), studied under Lama Jampa Thaye and others, and held posts at the British Library and SOAS University of London.
Samani Pratibha Pragya is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London, where she also worked as a research assistant (attested 2020).

Samdhong Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries. He held positions at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1971–2001) and Central Schools for Tibetans, among other organizations.

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Drepung Monastery, SOAS, and the University of London under David Snellgrove, he held posts at SOAS, CNRS (Directeur de Recherche from 1980), and Collège de France.

Samuel Beal was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA at Trinity College, Cambridge (circa 1843–1847), was headmaster at Bramham College (1848–1850), and served as Professor of Chinese at University College London from 1877.

Samuel George Frederick Brandon was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Leeds (circa 1930–1934) and held a post at the University of Manchester from circa 1951 to 1971.
Samuel Johnson was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College in Stourbridge (circa 1725–1726), and Pembroke College (1728–1731).
Samuel M. Grupper specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University, where he studied under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.
Samuel Wells Williams was a scholar in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (circa 1831–1832) and later held a post at Yale University from circa 1877 to 1884.

Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She held academic posts at San Diego State University, where she was attested as Professor in 1999 and Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014.
